content.title: About
content.content: Einkorn (the earliest cultivated wheat) is an ancient one‑year grass that yields whole grains rich in protein, fiber, and minerals. It is the first domesticated cereal, appearing more than 10,000 years ago in the Near East. In its dry form the grain has a nutty aroma and a slightly crunchy texture. It is used in cooking, baking, porridges and as a heritage alternative to modern wheat varieties.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Einkorn is considered the ancestor of modern wheat but retains a much simpler genetic makeup.
The grain contains more protein (about 15 %) and iron than common wheat.
Einkorn is often grown without synthetic fertilizers, making it popular among organic growers.
Unlike most modern varieties, einkorn’s gluten structure is thought to be more easily digestible.
Archaeological finds of einkorn date back to 9500 BC.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Einkorn provides roughly 15 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and immune function.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Phenolic compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Einkorn raises blood sugar more slowly, which can be beneficial for glycemic control.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Einkorn contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to grain proteins, including einkorn.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: As with any grain, non‑organic einkorn may carry pesticide residues; choose certified organic when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Einkorn can be boiled as a whole grain, added to soups, salads, or baked goods, or milled into flour for breads and pastries. Soaking the grains for 8–12 hours before cooking improves digestibility and reduces cooking time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry einkorn grains in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat oxidation.
